The bar is an Auto Layout row that hugs its declared controls (layoutContract); measured rects only check that the product formula closes. Breadcrumb labels before the last are auto-width inside a horizontal nav spaced by the product separator margin (4px); the last label fills the nav and truncates at the end, so a label set through a TEXT property reflows instead of clipping. The runner reports any auto-width default label whose Figma width differs from these bounds (glyphDrift).

$hairline.note: The measured border is the hairline as rasterized at device pixel ratio 1; Figma binds the declared token, so a hugging bar is padding + tallest child + the token value.

$bindingPolicy: Colors bind to the live LOUIS collections (Klipse Primitive[Base] · Klipse Semantic[Global] · Klipse Semantic Color[Light/Dark]); the retired 1 · Palette / 2 · Semantic are gone. The measured theme picks the pinned mode. bindingEvidence records measured value beside the live resolution; surface, divider and avatar ink must be exact.

$labelProperties: Both sets expose breadcrumb text as TEXT component properties named after the product mainChromePageNav fields: Single binds Label; Trail binds Parent and Current; the separator is not a property. A set-level TEXT property has one default, so every bound master text shows that default and existing instances without an override show it too. Consumers must set these properties from their measured labels.

layoutContract.$why: Product top bar declares no height: min-block-size 0 + padding 8 + tallest child + bottom hairline (layoutSources). So the variant hugs vertically; its default width is the measured bar and consumers set FILL. Leading and trailing clusters hug their declared controls; the breadcrumb nav fills the rest and truncates the last label.
